fundamental.thesis: Reliance Industries is India's largest conglomerate by market cap (₹17.5L cr), spanning O2C refining/petchem, digital services (Jio Platforms with 533mn subscribers), retail (RRVL), and new energy — per the Sector Card, SOTP/EV-EBITDA is the correct yardstick, not P/E. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew a strong +24.5% YoY to ₹3,40,257 cr with record quarterly EBITDA of ₹54,067 cr (+10.1% YoY), but PAT grew only +6.1% YoY to ₹23,196 cr as EBITDA margins contracted from 17.8% (FY26) to 15.9% (Q1FY27); retail PAT fell 14.2% YoY and finance costs surged 18.5% YoY to ₹8,337 cr from 5G asset capitalisation, confirming a margin-contracting trajectory even on accelerating revenues. EV/EBITDA of 12.2× sits at P83 vs Energy sector peers, but the peer set is dominated by policy-discounted PSU OMCs — Jio's 53.3% EBITDA margin, 20% digital revenue growth, a filed DRHP for Jio IPO, and forward P/E of 18.0× below trailing 21.7× collectively make the conglomerate premium fair rather than stretched; the stock at 1.7% of its 52-week range provides reasonable risk/reward. The primary risk is that surging finance costs and retail weakness keep consolidated PAT margin anchored at 6–7%, causing EPS growth to substantially lag revenue growth and disappoint the 26-analyst consensus which has revised FY estimates up +28.8% over 30 days.

HDFC Bank is India's largest private-sector bank (₹11.6L cr market cap), operating a fully integrated retail-lending franchise with 9,600+ branches, 100mn+ customers, and a strengthening mortgage book following the HDFC Ltd merger. Full-year FY26 revenue and PAT grew at +11.0% and +10.0% YoY respectively, showing mild acceleration from the 9M FY26 run-rate of +9.1%/+11.4%; credit quality improved materially with Gross NPA declining to 1.15% (from 1.24% in Q3FY26), PCR rising to 125%, and ROA recovering to 1.9%, though NIM at 3.35% (9M FY26, latest extracted) remains under pressure from asymmetric rate transmission. Using the appropriate P/B + ROE yardstick for banks per the sector card, a P/B of 2.0× against TTM ROE of 13.8% grades as fair — at the sector P/E median (P50 in peer set), though at a P/B premium to peer median (P79, +34.7% premium), which is partly justified by the quality gap vs PSU peers (CANBK, BANKINDIA); at 8.6% of its 52-week range the entry risk/reward is more favourable than the premium P/B alone implies. The primary risk is NIM remaining compressed longer than consensus expects — deposit repricing has caught up only 40–50bps vs full asset repricing, and sell-side EPS estimates have already been cut -5.6% in the past 30/90 days even before the Q1 FY27 results (earnings call intimated 2026-10-13) are fully digested.

H1 FY27 reported revenue accelerated sharply to +12.6% YoY (₹1,45,463 cr) versus FY26's stagnant +4.6%, with PAT up +9.6% to ₹27,354 cr and PAT margin expanding to 18.81% from the FY26 trough of 18.4% — critically, FY26 constant-currency growth was -2.4%, meaning INR depreciation has been a meaningful tailwind flattering the INR-denominated acceleration, and EBITDA margin has simultaneously contracted 82bps to 27.2% (H1 FY27 vs 28.0% H1 FY26), indicating real pricing and mix pressure. Trailing P/E of 16.3× sits 34% below the IT sector benchmark range (22–30×) and at P0 (cheapest in sector) on forward P/E vs 8 peers, with EV/EBITDA of 11.1× also 24% below the peer median — both primary IT valuation yardsticks point to unambiguously cheap, anchored further by a pristine net-cash balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA of -0.05, interest coverage 70.7×) and a 51% ROE that justifies the elevated 7.1× P/B. The principal risk is that INR strengthening (trend: 94.96, strengthening per today's macro) unwinds the FX tailwind that is inflating reported INR growth, while declining deferred revenue (₹9,402 cr → ₹8,310 cr) and persistent downward EPS revisions (-0.6% 30d, -0.8% next-FY) signal the AI-deflation pressure on legacy IT spend has not yet been offset by new AI-native deal flow — a falling-knife dynamic near the 52-week low that demands patience.

ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private sector bank by assets, running a diversified franchise across retail lending, wholesale banking, and listed subsidiaries (ICICI Life, ICICI Lombard, ICICI Prudential AMC). Q1FY27 delivered NII growth of +12.7% YoY to ₹24,384 crore, PAT up +12.6% YoY to ₹16,276 crore with loan book accelerating to +19.6% YoY — though total income growth decelerated from +9.2% to +6.9% QoQ, the sector KPIs that matter for banks are directionally sound: NIM stable at 4.36% (up from 4.34% year-ago), gross NPA improving to 1.38% from 1.67% a year ago, and ROA rising to 2.43%. Applying the sector card's P/B+ROE yardstick, valuation is fair — P/B 2.48× against ROE 16.4% sits above the cheap threshold (P/B <1.5) but well below expensive (P/B >3 with ROE <12%), and trailing P/E 16.82× lands squarely within the 12–18× bank sector benchmark; at P93 on both forward P/E and P/B versus 14 banking peers the quality premium is baked in but leaves limited re-rating runway. The biggest risk is a structural deterioration: CASA ratio declined sharply to 38.1% from 41.4% sequentially, weakening the low-cost deposit franchise, while credit costs spiked 10× QoQ to 31bps — partially RBI-mandated but a pattern worth watching — and Q2FY27 results are being presented today (earnings call 5pm IST, 1 unread filing), making the Q1FY27 data one quarter stale with fresh surprises possible.

Using P/B + ROE as the prescribed NBFC yardstick (sector card): P/B of 2.56× with ROE 16.4% is fair; trailing P/E of 16.83× sits just below the NBFC sector lower bound of 18×, forward P/E 12.9× signals continued earnings growth ahead, and peer rank P33–P44 confirms a ~16% discount to sector median — overall graded fair with a cheap lean. 3M India is the Indian subsidiary of 3M USA, operating across four diversified industrials segments — Safety & Industrial, Transportation & Electronics, Healthcare, and Consumer — with MNC-grade governance under a 75.86% foreign promoter and no promoter-pledge risk. Revenue growth accelerated to +19.0% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹1,423cr), the fifth consecutive double-digit quarter with all four segments growing 13–24%, but underlying earnings quality is deteriorating: EBITDA fell 2.7% YoY (margin contracting 360 bps YoY to 17.6% from 21.2%), PBT before exceptional items declined 4.3% YoY, and the headline PAT of ₹233cr (+31% YoY) was materially inflated by a one-time ₹73.13cr land-sale gain — strip that out and underlying PAT margin is roughly 12–13%, not 16.4%. At a trailing P/E of 64×, the stock trades at an 82% premium to the broad-market median and well above the Industrials sector benchmark of 28–45×; EV/EBITDA of 36.45× likewise screens expensive even versus richly-valued capital-goods peers, making the valuation grade unambiguously expensive despite the forward P/E of 42.2× signalling some earnings recovery priced in. INR depreciation is the primary operating headwind — 3M India is structurally import-dependent on the parent's global supply chain, and a weakening rupee directly compresses margins; with D/E at 9.6 and finance costs already up 86% YoY, any further currency weakness or rate uptick compounds the derating risk at a 64× entry.
